name: Distributed Key-Value Store (DynamoDB-Style)
description: Design a distributed key-value store like DynamoDB or Riak. Covers consistent hashing, replication, vector clocks, and tunable consistency.

learnSteps.title: Consistent Hashing and Partitioning
learnSteps.description: Keys are mapped to a hash ring using consistent hashing. Each storage node owns a range of the ring. Virtual nodes (vnodes) ensure even distribution — each physical node has ~256 vnodes. When a node joins/leaves, only keys in adjacent ranges are redistributed, minimizing data movement.

learnSteps.title: Coordinator and Quorum Reads/Writes
learnSteps.description: The Coordinator Node receives each request and determines which N storage nodes own the key. For a write, it sends the value to all N replicas and waits for W acknowledgments (quorum write). For a read, it queries N replicas and waits for R responses. With N=3, W=2, R=2, you get strong consistency (W+R > N).

learnSteps.title: Replication and Hinted Handoff
learnSteps.description: Each key is replicated to N successor nodes on the hash ring. If a replica is temporarily down, the coordinator sends the write to a healthy node with a 'hint' — the intended destination. When the failed node recovers, hints are replayed from the queue. This achieves high availability even during failures.

learnSteps.title: LSM-Tree Storage Engine
learnSteps.description: Each storage node uses an LSM-tree: writes go to an in-memory MemTable, then flush to sorted SSTables on disk. Reads check the MemTable, then Bloom filters on SSTables to skip irrelevant files. Compaction merges SSTables in the background. This design optimizes for write-heavy workloads.

chaosScenarios.name: Storage Node Network Partition
chaosScenarios.description: A network partition isolates one replica of an N=3 replica group from its peers
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: With W=2, writes still succeed via sloppy quorum — hinted handoffs accumulate in the hint queue for the unreachable node. R=1 reads may return stale values. On heal, hint replay and read repair reconcile divergent versions using vector clocks.
mitigationSteps: Confirm sloppy quorum is accepting writes and hints are queueing
Monitor hint queue depth against its TTL bound
On partition heal, verify hinted handoff replay completes
Schedule Merkle-tree anti-entropy repair to catch anything hints missed

chaosScenarios.name: Coordinator Node Crash
chaosScenarios.description: A coordinator node crashes mid-request while orchestrating quorum reads and writes
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: The request router redistributes traffic to surviving coordinators within seconds. In-flight requests fail; SDKs retry idempotently against a new coordinator. Brief p99 spike, no data loss — coordinators are stateless.
mitigationSteps: Verify the router has ejected the dead coordinator from rotation
Confirm SDK retries succeeded (no client-visible error spike)
Check that per-coordinator load is balanced after re-admission

chaosScenarios.name: Partition Map Metadata DB Outage
chaosScenarios.description: The metadata DB holding the partition map becomes unavailable
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Reads and writes continue normally — coordinators serve from their cached ring. Cluster membership changes (node joins, leaves, rebalancing) are blocked. Risk grows over time: if topology changes while the map is stale, requests get misrouted.
mitigationSteps: Freeze all membership changes and rebalancing operations
Confirm coordinators are serving from cached partition maps within TTL
Restore the metadata DB from its replica
Reconcile ring version across coordinators before re-enabling membership changes

bottleneckProgression.description: DAX item cache eviction churn — working set exceeds memory and the hit rate drop pushes reads to storage nodes
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Scale the cache cluster, tune item TTLs, and pin hot keys

bottleneckProgression.description: LSM compaction falls behind under write load; read amplification grows and p99 reads spike
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Add storage nodes to re-shard the ring, move to faster NVMe, rate-limit compaction I/O

bottleneckProgression.description: Coordinator CPU saturates on quorum coordination, serialization, and vector clock bookkeeping
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Scale coordinators horizontally behind the request router

expectedIssues.title: Hot Partition From Key Skew
expectedIssues.description: Skewed access patterns concentrate traffic on one partition's replica group, saturating it while the rest of the ring idles
expectedIssues.mitigation: Key salting, adaptive partition splitting, and DAX caching absorbing hot-key reads

expectedIssues.title: Vector Clock Sibling Explosion
expectedIssues.description: Concurrent writes during partitions produce many divergent versions of the same key, pushing merge complexity onto clients
expectedIssues.mitigation: Cap sibling counts, use last-write-wins for low-value keys, CRDTs or server-side merge for the rest

expectedIssues.title: LSM Compaction Backlog
expectedIssues.description: Sustained write bursts outpace compaction; SSTable counts grow and read p99 degrades across the ring
expectedIssues.mitigation: Rate-limit compaction I/O, schedule major compactions off-peak, alert on pending-SSTable counts

expectedIssues.title: Hint Queue Overflow on Extended Outage
expectedIssues.description: A node down longer than the hint TTL leaves handoff incomplete; consistency then depends on slow anti-entropy repair
expectedIssues.mitigation: Bound hint TTL explicitly, alert on queue depth, and always run Merkle-tree repair after extended outages

expectedIssues.title: Stale Reads at R=1
expectedIssues.description: Latency-optimized R=1 reads can return values that predate the latest acknowledged write within the replication window
expectedIssues.mitigation: Expose tunable consistency — clients use R+W>N on read-your-writes paths and R=1 elsewhere

components.label: Metadata DB (Partition Map)
components.costDriver: Small HA pair — tiny data, high criticality

metrics.name: pending_compactions

metrics.description: Ring topology version served by metadata DB

steps: Determine whether the node is dead or partitioned (avoid replacing a partitioned node)
Verify sloppy quorum is serving writes and hints are accumulating within TTL
Replace the node and stream its ranges from replica peers
Replay hints, then run read repair / Merkle-tree anti-entropy
Confirm ring rebalance completed and per-node load is even
Identify hot keys via per-partition request metrics
Enable DAX caching for the hot keys to absorb reads
Split the partition or work with the app team to salt keys
Verify replica group utilization returns to fleet median
Freeze membership changes and rebalancing immediately
Confirm coordinators serve from cached ring within map TTL
Restore the metadata DB from its standby replica
Reconcile partition map versions across all coordinators before unfreezing

decisions.title: Consistent Hashing With Virtual Nodes
decisions.context: The store must scale incrementally — adding capacity cannot require rehashing the whole keyspace
decisions.decision: Keys map onto a hash ring; each physical node owns many virtual nodes, with the partition map stored in a metadata DB
consequences: Adding a node moves only ~1/N of the data
Virtual node counts balance heterogeneous hardware
The partition map becomes critical metadata that must be cached and versioned

decisions.title: Tunable Quorum (N, R, W)
decisions.context: Different workloads on the same store need different consistency/latency points
decisions.decision: Replicate each key to N nodes; clients choose R and W per request
consequences: R+W>N yields read-your-writes; R=1 yields fastest reads with staleness risk
Consistency becomes an application-level dial rather than a fixed property
Operators must monitor quorum failures as a first-class signal

decisions.title: Sloppy Quorum With Hinted Handoff
decisions.context: The system must remain writeable through individual node failures and short partitions
decisions.decision: Writes fall back to healthy fallback nodes that hold hints, replayed to the home replica on recovery
consequences: Divergent versions require vector clocks, read repair, and anti-entropy
Hint TTL and queue depth define the recovery-consistency boundary

decisions.title: LSM-Tree Storage Engine
decisions.context: Write-heavy KV workloads punish in-place B-tree updates
decisions.decision: Storage nodes use log-structured merge trees with memtables, SSTables, and background compaction
consequences: Writes are sequential appends — high sustained write throughput
Reads pay amplification across SSTable levels, mitigated by bloom filters
Compaction is a permanent background tax that must be capacity-planned

tradeoffs.choice: Availability under partition (AP) — accept writes via sloppy quorum
tradeoffs.benefit: No write downtime through node failures and short partitions
tradeoffs.cost: Eventual consistency: stale reads, version siblings, and repair machinery

tradeoffs.benefit: Sequential-I/O writes sustain high throughput cheaply
tradeoffs.cost: Read amplification across levels, bounded by bloom filters and compaction discipline

alternatives.name: Single-Leader Replication
alternatives.description: One primary accepts all writes and ships them to replicas (classic RDBMS topology)
alternatives.prosVsCons: Strong, simple consistency — but the leader caps write throughput and failover means write downtime
alternatives.whyNotChosen: The target workload demands always-on writes and linear horizontal write scaling

alternatives.name: Per-Partition Consensus (Raft/Paxos)
alternatives.description: Each partition runs a consensus group providing linearizable reads and writes
alternatives.prosVsCons: Linearizability without client-side merging, but every write pays cross-replica round trips and leader elections cause availability dips
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Latency and availability targets favor the Dynamo-style AP design; apps that need stronger guarantees use R+W>N
